title: Revise token contrast ramps and radius hierarchy for dense data fabric
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Update and rationalize color contrast ramps, typography scale, spacing and radius tokens, and elevation/shadow layers specifically for dense data surfaces (tables, line charts, small cards) so compact UIs maintain legibility, hierarchy, and accessible contrast at smaller sizes.
background: Recent QA and customer feedback highlight uneven contrast and cramped rhythm in compact tables and chart legends after the 2025 token reshuffle. Small type + tight spacing causes visual noise and reduces perceived separation between rows and annotations. We have separate token sets for core surfaces but lack a clearly defined dense-data token variant and a documented radius/elevation hierarchy for 8px and below contexts.
goal: Deliver a coherent set of token adjustments and usage guidance that: 1) raises accessible contrast for body and caption text in compact components; 2) defines spacing and corner radius tiers for dense layouts; 3) rebalances elevation/shadow to improve perceived separation without increasing visual clutter; 4) ship as a backwards-compatible tokens minor release with migration notes.
proposed_changes: Introduce a 'dense' token alias group (e.g., surface.dense-*/text.dense-*) with explicit contrast targets (WCAG AA minimum for caption/body at 12px/13px).
Add two new radius tokens: radius.xs-2 (2px) and radius.xs-4 (4px) and map compact components to xs-2/xs-4 rather than reusing base radii.
Adjust typography scale: bump caption from 12px 400 to 12px 500 in dense contexts to improve legibility on low-DPI screens and mobile 2x rendering quirks.

Create a 'separation' elevation token set that uses subtle linear shadows and 1px hairline separators for rows; reduce blur and opacity on deepest shadows used on full-size cards to avoid heavy contrast in dense lists.
Define spacing tokens for dense grids (gap.dense-1 = 4px, gap.dense-2 = 8px) and map table row-height variants to those tokens with examples.
Publish migration guide including token mapping table, recommended CSS variables, and an automated codemod for common component usages.
Add a visual QA checklist and sample dataset-driven storybook stories for tables/charts at small sizes.
Run accessibility contrast checks across primary browsers and in the in-house screenshot regression harness.
Coordinate with engineering to add flags for runtime 'compact' variant so teams can toggle during rollout.
Provide design tokens JSON and Figma token library updates and link to implementation PRs.
Measure perceptual improvements via user QA and telemetry for interaction regressions (click target, hover areas).
acceptance_criteria: Dense token aliases exist in tokens JSON and are loaded by the design token loader
Compact components (Table.smallRow, Chart.legendCompact, MiniCard) updated to reference new radius and spacing tokens
Automated contrast reports show caption/body in dense surfaces meet WCAG AA at target sizes on tested browsers
Storybook has new dense component stories with real dataset and visual snapshots committed
Migration guide published with token mapping table and example codemod instructions
Frontend PRs merged with feature flag for gradual rollout and no regressions in core flows detected by CI visual diff suite
implementation_notes: Coordinate with ENG runtime team to ensure token resolver supports variant aliases (tokens['text.dense-1'] -> value)
Prefer CSS variables with fallback to existing tokens to avoid runtime undefined states
Keep base token names unchanged; add dense aliases and document preferred usage to minimize breakages
Codemod should target common patterns: TableRow class, .chart-legend .label, MiniCard border-radius usage
Plan for a two-week canary: opt-in teams roll to flag, then enable platform-wide after monitoring
